claims.text: Capital grants are available for charities working with disability.
The grants support new buildings, refurbishment, or equipment.
The purpose of the funding is to increase independence, training, employment, and supported housing for people with disability.
The minimum capital cost for a project is £50,000.
There must be a shortfall in capital funding of at least £25,000.
The minimum grant amount is £25,000.
The usual grant range is £40,000 to £75,000.
Applicants must be registered charities or local authorities.
If applicable, organizations should have at least a ‘Good’ rating from a regulator such as CQC or Ofsted.
Projects must address at least one of the following aims: increased access to services, improved quality and range of services, or improved future sustainability of the organization.
The application process involves two stages.
Stage 1 applications are submitted via an online system and require a brief project description, total cost, funding shortfall, proposed timetable, and confirmation of Chief Executive support.
Audited accounts for the past two years are required for Stage 1 applications.
Stage 2 applications are by invitation only.
At least 25% of capital costs must be raised before submitting a Stage 2 application, unless the project cost is under £80,000.
Necessary planning permission should be in place for Stage 2 applications.
Organizations that have previously received a grant must wait five years before applying again for a different project, unless they are universities or large charities with multiple sites.
Organizations turned down at Stage 1 can submit a new application for a different project at any time.
Organizations turned down at Stage 2 must wait at least one year before submitting a new application for a different project.
The same project will not normally be considered twice.
There are two funding rounds each year.
For Round 1, Stage 1 applications open on November 20th and the deadline is January 5th.
For Round 1, Stage 2 application deadline is March 1st.
For Round 2, Stage 1 applications open on May 14th and the deadline is July 1st.
For Round 2, Stage 2 application deadline is September 1st.
Funding decisions are made in June and December annually.
If a deadline falls on a weekend, applications are accepted by 9 am on the following Monday.
Grants are not made retrospectively, and projects must be ongoing at the time of a funding decision.
An invitation to Stage 2 remains open for three funding rounds unless otherwise agreed.
The funding is for UK applicants only.
